description: Windows Server and container base image reference for BF system legacy migration

host_os_versions.notes: Current BF ATOM dev / target host OS. EOL Jan 2020. No security patches.
host_os_versions.container_host_note: Cannot run Docker containers natively without Hyper-V; EOL in any case

host_os_versions.container_host: Yes — Windows containers; Linux containers via Hyper-V isolation
host_os_versions.notes: First Windows version with native container support.
Recommended if Windows container host is required for BF .NET Fx components.

host_os_versions.container_host: Yes — recommended; eBPF support, improved container networking
host_os_versions.notes: Best current option for Windows containers.

windows_container_base_images.use_case: C++, .NET Fx, legacy apps needing full Windows APIs
windows_container_base_images.notes: Full Server Core. Largest but most compatible.
Includes IIS + ASP.NET. Recommended for C# broker IIS deployments.
No IIS. For Windows Service-style C# components.
Much smaller than Server Core but very limited API surface. NOT suitable for .NET Fx.

host_container_version_compatibility.note: Windows container image version MUST match or be older than the container host OS version.
host_container_version_compatibility.implication_for_bf: If target K8s Windows node runs WS2019, use ltsc2019 images. If WS2022, use ltsc2022.

YAJSW.container_replacement: Translate wrapper.conf JVM args to Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT

Tanuki_JSW.notes: Commercial product; same conf format as YAJSW

NSSM.container_replacement: Use ENTRYPOINT with the wrapped executable directly
NSSM.extraction: On WS2008 R2: nssm dump <ServiceName> > service-config.txt

WinSW.container_replacement: Extract arguments from XML; use as ENTRYPOINT args
